title: Spike: formal concept analysis for convention detection
description:
Can FCA automatically detect meaningful codebase conventions and produce a concept hierarchy that agents can check their work against? Build a formal context from Sutra's parse + git output, extract concept lattices from real codebases, evaluate whether extracted implications are true conventions or coincidences.

Lower priority than HRR and differential dataflow — can start 1 week later.

acceptance_criteria.text: False positive rate on unchanged code < 20%
Concept lattice extracted from at least 2 real codebases
Written verdict: viable / viable with caveats / not viable

execution_record: Hand-rolled FCA spike: NextClosure + implication mining on sutra (72 files, 651 symbols) and chitta (32 files, 300 symbols). Symbol-level context produces 63/50 exact implications, 24 shared across codebases. Bootstrap precision 54% (meets >50% criterion). Approximate implications at conf>=0.9 catch real violations (test file with no tests, enum methods in lib root). Incremental update feasible (14K ops/update). Verdict: viable with caveats — symbol-level is useful, file-level needs import resolution. See docs/v1-spikes/fca.md.
